# Public Content Publishing

チャット用スキルの正本はMy Portal DBの`chatSkills/public-content-publishing`。以下は過去のMethod指示から一回だけ移管した初期本文。以後は旧Methodを優先して使わない。必要な外部情報は対応するOperatorで取得する。

1) Start from an actual conversation, Thinking Space idea, memo, artifact, or research result. Do not invent a content topic merely to satisfy SEO.
2) Before drafting, classify source material into PUBLIC-SAFE and PRIVATE. PRIVATE always includes: the user's or any private person's real name when not intentionally public, personal email/phone/address, exact home/work/school location when it can identify a person, account/customer/member IDs, birth date or uniquely identifying biographical combinations, non-public employment/financial/legal/health/family details, passwords, API keys/tokens/cookies/session IDs, private URLs containing credentials/tokens, private repository/infrastructure identifiers, internal IDs, sourceRefs, raw provenance, and any fact that materially increases the ability to identify or contact a private person.
3) Public output must be data-minimized. If an identifying detail is not essential, delete it. If context is useful but identity is not, generalize it (for example "a prior workplace", "a private project", "a conversation") rather than pseudonymizing with a reversible clue.
4) Never infer that a detail is safe merely because it appeared in a prior ChatGPT conversation, My Portal, a connected app, a file, sourceRefs, seoResearch, or model memory. Those are private inputs by default.
5) Extract a self-contained public unit only from the PUBLIC-SAFE subset. Preserve provenance only in private Public CMS fields; never copy private IDs or source notes into title, summary, body, tags, SEO metadata, diagrams, image alt text, structured data, or URLs.
6) Choose the target public site based on subject fit.
7) Use Keywords Operator only to test a small number of natural search-entry formulations around the existing idea. Do not let keyword demand replace or distort the idea.
8) Select at most one primaryKeyword, a few secondaryKeywords, searchIntent, SEO title and description. If no credible search demand/intent exists, publish as a non-SEO note or keep draft; do not manufacture keywords.
9) Create/update a Public CMS draft with private provenance in sourceRefs and raw keyword evidence in seoResearch.
10) Run a semantic privacy review over every public-facing field: title, summary, bodyMarkdown, tags, keyTakeaways, locale/translation metadata that is exposed, SEO title/description/canonical path, diagrams, tables, links, image references/alt text, and structured data generated by the frontend. Check both direct identifiers and combinations of quasi-identifiers. Check Japanese and English versions independently.
11) Also rely on the CMS deterministic privacy scanner for common secrets and identifiers. Passing the scanner is necessary but not sufficient; semantic review remains mandatory.
12) If any questionable personal or secret detail remains, do not Publish. Redact/generalize it first. When uncertain, keep it private.
13) Publish only via public_content_publish so the published snapshot/revision boundary and deploy hook are preserved.
14) Frontends consume only the anonymous published projection and must not inject author names or other personal identity metadata unless the user separately and explicitly opts that specific identity field into publication.

15) Treat every published content object as an ordinary note whose shape may evolve over time. Do not create a separate "Living Page", "database page", or parallel content class for this behavior.
16) Keep bodyMarkdown as the normal narrative layer and backward-compatible default. A note with no blocks remains a normal static-looking note.
17) Add blocks only when the note benefits from structure that will be updated independently of the prose:
- summary: current state / current conclusion, usually before-body.
- dataset: changing records or comparisons. Use declared scalar columns only; choose table/cards/matrix/tracker as a view, not as a new page type.
- timeline: meaningful changes, experiments, decisions, or revisions over time.
- diagram: structural/relational visual support using Mermaid.
- markdown: additional narrative that needs to sit apart from the legacy/main body.
18) Use placement=before-body for orientation/current snapshot and placement=after-body for datasets, history, appendices, and supporting structure unless the reading flow clearly calls for another order.
19) Prefer human-readable rendering over database aesthetics. On small screens, datasets should be readable as cards rather than squeezed tables. Structured blocks must support the prose, not turn the note into an admin UI.
20) A note may gain, lose, or change blocks across revisions without changing its conceptual identity, slug, translation group, or URL. Revision history records the change.
21) Privacy review applies to every structured block and every dataset record exactly as it applies to prose. Do not hide private data inside a dataset, timeline, diagram, or block metadata.

22) Treat narrative coherence as a publication gate. A reader should be able to move through one cognitive path without repeatedly restarting the article.
23) Before Publish, identify the note's single primary question or claim. Arrange the prose around a natural sequence such as problem → realization → approach → implications → current practice. Do not give equal top-level weight to unrelated concerns merely because the data exists.
24) Avoid repeated orientation layers. Summary, key takeaways, current snapshot, introduction, and callouts must not restate the same point several times before the article begins. Keep only the minimum orientation needed.
25) Introduce domain-specific product/tool names only after the reader understands their role conceptually. Prefer "private thinking layer" before "My Portal", "public snapshot" before "Public CMS", etc., when the proper noun would otherwise increase cognitive load.
26) Structured blocks remain subordinate to the narrative. Implementation datasets, changelogs, and operational metadata should usually appear after the main argument unless they are necessary to understand the next paragraph.
27) Separate conceptual explanation from implementation detail. A note may explain the idea first and then provide "current implementation" / "change history" as supporting material.
28) Heading hierarchy should reflect abstraction levels. Do not mix a high-level conceptual section, a low-level component list, an SEO note, and an operational changelog as sibling sections unless they are genuinely equal parts of the argument.
29) For translations, preserve the cognitive path rather than translating section-by-section mechanically. The English version may rephrase transitions, headings, or examples to remain natural while preserving meaning.
30) Final narrative review question: "If all datasets, timelines, SEO metadata, and implementation names were temporarily hidden, would the prose still make sense as a coherent note?" If not, revise before Publish.

## v5: 読者起点の編集・初見テスト（全公開記事に適用）

**記事の可読性は、正しい用語説明や見出しを少し追加するだけでは達成できない。本文全体の認知的な順序を組み直す。** 出典・privacy・CMS publishの既存規則はすべて維持する。

31) Antonbase Notesの編集正本 https://github.com/nomuonji/antonbase-notes/blob/main/docs/EDITORIAL_STANDARD.md を読む。repoへアクセスできない場合も、以下の品質契約を省略しない。
32) 下書き前に非公開のReader Contractを作る：想定読者と前提知識／入口となる困りごと／読み終わったとき説明できる一つのこと／本文を通して使う具体例／今回扱わないこと／事実と推測の境界。初見は現会話や私有システムの名称を**知らない**ものとする。
33) 記事を「実装・技術解説」「考察・エッセイ」「参照ノート」に分類し、タイプに応じた読書順序を設計する。すべてを一つの問題→解決テンプレートに機械的に当てはめない。
34) 技術解説は原則、具体的問題→必要最小限の前提→**同じ具体例を追跡**して入力・判断・操作・結果→設計選択→短い実装例→確認済みの限界の順。概念や内部名称を知る前の読者に「Macro Policy」「Sites Operator」「Planner role」等を一度に投げない。
35) 同じ主張をsummary・導入・複数の章・図・結論で反復しない。各節は前節の理解を前進させる。内部運用の時系列、PR番号、バージョン、枝葉のトラブルは、主題に不可欠な場合以外は補足へ。
36) 初出の専門語と固有名詞は機能と実体を平易な一文で定義してから使う。アクターとソフトウェアとAPI上のrole名を混同しない。コード例・JSON・図は「なぜ今必要か」を一文で説明し、単独で読めなくても本文は成立させる。
37) 直前の文章を付け足しで直すだけの改稿は原則禁止。**削除・統合・見出し順序の変更・段落の作り直し**を必須の編集候補として検討する。要点を残したまま文章量を削減し、不要な繰り返しやメタな前置きを除く。
38) 本文完成後に全文を通読して初見テストを行う：(a) タイトル・要約・初めの2段落で対象と問題が分かる、(b) 初見でも一つの事例の問題→判断→実装→確認を追える、(c) 未説明語を調べずに次段落を読める、(d) 見出しのみで論旨が進展する、(e) 不要な節や重複段落を削れる、(f) 実装済み／計画／未検証が正確、(g) 内部固有名を使わず読み手に内容を言い返せる。
39) フロントエンドではタイトル→summary→任意のkeyTakeaways/summaryブロック→本文の順に表示される。**summaryと本文冒頭が同じ説明を繰り返していない**か、CMS実表示順で確認する。
40) 初見テストに落ちた場合は公開禁止。段落を足すのではなくReader Contract・具体例・章構成からやり直す。必要ならdraftで止めて問題と直すべき場所を報告する。合格を判断できないまま「公開完了・読みやすい」と断言しない。
41) 公開後にページの見え方、見出し、mobileの表・図を確認できるなら確認する。CMS公開snapshotが確認できてもライブ画面を検証できないなら「CMS公開済み／フロント表示は未検証」と明記する。

## v6: server-enforced editorial handoff (all Public CMS publishing)

42) Before writing, call `method_get_context(id="TbvbUVFjkC2xPAbNqU2Q")` and read the active Method in full. Do not infer prior instructions from memory; the current Method is the source of truth. Read the per-site editorial standard and create the private Reader Contract.
43) Write and structurally edit the complete draft. Before publishing, after all changes, call `public_content_editorial_prepare(siteId,slug)`. **Read its returned current active Method instructions and quality gates**; if the active version has changed since drafting, redo the editorial review. The prepare response gives the draft-bound `reviewId`.
44) Re-read the final draft as a first-time reader and perform: Reader Contract, coherent section order, a continuous concrete example or justified reference format, glossary-on-first-use, whole-article deletion/rewrite pass, evidence/unknown classification and semantic privacy inspection.
45) Call `public_content_editorial_approve` with the prepared reviewId, all seven checked items, a substantive reviewNotes field (80+ characters), a functional reviewer name such as `chatgpt_editor`, and confirm=true. Only mark true for an actual completed review. The backend verifies the current draft fingerprint and active Method version; false or missing checks fail closed. No semantic score is implied.
46) Call `public_content_privacy_scan` then `public_content_publish`. The backend **refuses publication** if it has no matching unexpired editorial review or if the draft/Method has changed. Do not attempt a bypass, direct database write or alternative publish route.
47) If prepare or approve is unavailable due to stale MCP connector schema, inability to read the Method, tool/deployment errors, or insufficient review evidence: save the draft and stop without publishing. Report the exact blocker. Connector refresh may be necessary once the new tools deploy.
48) Source of the publish-gate code and recovery contract: https://github.com/nomuonji/my-portal/blob/main/docs/PUBLIC_CMS_EDITORIAL_GATE.md . Required for ALL Public CMS sites, independent of which publication frontend consumes the published snapshot.

## v7: the writing session starts before any CMS draft content

49) **Before** calling `public_content_create` or `public_content_update` with public-facing content, call `public_content_editorial_prepare(siteId,slug)` and read the complete active Method instructions. This works for a slug that does not yet exist: `mode=begin_writing` means the writing contract has been loaded. For an existing draft the mode is `review_draft`.
50) Pass that tool's `reviewId` to the create/update API as `editorialSessionId`. The backend now requires a matching site/slug, unexpired and active Method version for EVERY public-facing draft create/edit. If the connector has not refreshed to expose the argument or prepare tool, **do not begin CMS writing**; refresh/reconnect instead of bypassing.
51) For edits, a prepared session authorizes the writing step, but NOT the final publication. After the LAST content edit, call prepare again to get the SHA-256 fingerprint of the finished draft, then complete the seven-item semantic review and approve. A changed draft invalidates its previous review receipt.
52) This is a two-stage source-of-truth requirement: an editorial session before drafting, a draft-bound editorial approval before publishing. Both read the ACTIVE My Portal Method. Never treat a previously remembered Method or this hardcoded prompt fragment as an alternative source of truth.

## v8: Public media relevance and internal-record separation (mandatory, site-aware)
53) BEFORE writing for a public media site, perform an **external audience relevance assessment** separate from readability: What question does an outsider bring, what does this article let them understand or decide, and why is this subject worthy of publication rather than an internal memo? A readable internal report is still not a publishable article.
54) For siteId `antonbase-notes`, read the current editorial charter at https://github.com/nomuonji/antonbase-notes/blob/main/docs/EDITORIAL_CHARTER.md **in addition to** https://github.com/nomuonji/antonbase-notes/blob/main/docs/EDITORIAL_STANDARD.md . Treat this site's identity as a reader-facing publication about technology, culture and knowledge—not a log of chat sessions or automation operations.
55) Distinguish source material and published subject: conversations, implementation histories and research ledgers are source/provenance; the published story must stand on its own for an unknown reader. If the only reason to publish is "we discussed or implemented it", keep it in a private Space/Project/Method, not Public CMS.
56) The public article's outline and headings follow the reader's questions. Strip internal-only context such as obsolete API role aliases, task or branch delivery lifecycle details, schedule frequency, internal management reorganizations, revision/PR history, or troubleshooting unrelated to the reader's primary question. First try **deleting** irrelevant details rather than defining them more carefully. Keep internal details only in explicit, valuable and independently readable case studies.
57) Avoid automatically converting every engineering conversation into a technical implementation report. Choose the reader-facing genre (explainer, evidence-led comparison, essay, research note, case study) according to public value; one conversation may yield no article.
58) In the private Reader Contract include a separate `externalReaderValue` and `internalDetailsToOmit`. For Antonbase Notes, the seven existing editorial review checks include this requirement: `readerContract=true` only after external value is established; `narrativeStructure=true` only after irrelevant internal narrative has been removed. In `reviewNotes`, record the public question, the value delivered and which internal context was removed. Do not falsely attest if these checks are missing.
59) For site positioning and home copy, talk to readers about topics and ideas they can explore, not about the author's chat archive or internal workflow. SEO metadata must likewise promise reader value rather than operation-report recency.
60) This editorial relevance gate does NOT loosen privacy checks, invalidate the existing pre-write `editorialSessionId`, or replace final-draft fingerprint approval. The active Method remains mandatory for all sites; Antonbase Notes adds the site-specific public media charter.
